why: Finding the first occurrence is the 'first index where nums[i] >= target' search (lower bound), plus one check that the value there really is the target.
hints: A normal binary search stops at any copy of the target. You want the leftmost one.
Search for the first index whose value is >= target. Every copy of target, if any, starts there.
lo, hi = 0, n; while lo < hi: mid >= target -> hi = mid else lo = mid + 1. Return lo if lo < n and nums[lo] == target, else -1. This is bisect_left.
pitfalls: lo can end at n when target is bigger than everything: check before reading nums[lo].
Stopping as soon as nums[mid] == target returns a middle copy, not the first.
